chapter: The Grid (levels 71-80, the neon wireframe world of mathematical solids) - regenerated on the desert's ember model (the owner, 2026-10-11, #824): a lead line the ear can follow, its identity in the mid range, the drive carried by arrangement rather than by noise and sub bass; the family's electronic dance root kept
purpose: Master of Game/Music/pulse-piano-house.ogg: written from this file by Tools/MusicBake --tracks --masters <this folder>, brought to the themes' loudness, peaks held under full scale, Ogg Vorbis. The master stays outside the repository (C:/Users/panrd/AI/output/masters-824-chosen on the desktop, with its .raw.wav; every candidate in masters-824); this sidecar is committed beside the .ogg.
generator: ACE-Step 1.5 (acestep.cpp v0.0.5), local, AMD RX 6900 XT via Vulkan -- batch-pulse.ps1 -> generate-music.ps1 -Loop -NoCotCaption
format: 48000 Hz, 32-bit float PCM, stereo -- 48 kHz is the model's fixed native rate

request.caption: 1990s piano house instrumental for a neon wireframe world of glowing geometric shapes: a catchy, memorable chord riff and melody you can hum on a warm, mellow grand piano, loud and upfront in the mid range, a warm analog synth lead answering the piano, a bouncing warm bass line, a tight warm four-on-the-floor kick, a deep round snare and warm toms playing throughout from the first bar, soft dark percussion, warm organ chords, building into a big joyful peak where the piano and the lead play the hook together, euphoric and uplifting, warm mid-forward mix, modern polished production with soft, warm, rolled-off highs, wide stereo mix with instruments panned left and right, stereo delays, spacious reverb, no vocals

chosen.why: replaces big room with 1990s piano house. Inside ember on every column: 13.2 % in 200 Hz-2 kHz, 9.5 % in 300 Hz-4 kHz, 0.8 % above 6 kHz, tonal mid 62 %, 4.23 held-note changes/s, a 46 s loop in time (context 0.81, crossfade r 0.90 against 0.93, spectrum cos 0.85), no hole, wrap step +8.0 dB (p82). The bright house piano kept eight of the first nine renders at 2.2-5.0 % above 6 kHz whatever the drums were; round 4's warm, mellow grand piano gave 1.8 % and 0.8 % (a Rhodes 5.0 % and 2.9 %). c10, first by a tenth of a point in 300 Hz-4 kHz, is a 32 s loop with a weak seam (context 0.36, spectrum cos 0.41)
chosen.how: every candidate measured with Tools/Generation/measure-music.py --reference ember in one run (band shares, tonal mid, mid flatness, held-note changes, tempo wander, wrap step) beside the loop cut's own check, the hole share (the loop more than 10 dB under its loud level), the breakdown dip and the stereo correlation; a seam below its own rhythm, a hole over 15 %, a 2 s dropout more than 20 dB down, a wrap step of 10 dB or more or at or above p97 of the loop's own steps, a seam spectrum cosine under 0.3 or a loop under 30 s ruled a candidate out; the table is on #824
